claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in HEAs is governed by the dynamic formation and maintenance of a mechanically adaptive passive film.
The multicomponent microstructure of HEAs sustains the mechanically adaptive passive film.
Minor phase transformations at the wear interface enable continuous reformation of the passive film.
Continuous film reformation enhances passivation during mechanical degradation.
The proposed test material is an equimolar or near-equimolar HEA with a predominantly single-phase, potentially FCC, matrix and a metastable microstructure.
Minor phase transformations and localized oxidation influence the composition and nanostructure of the regenerating passive film.
The continuously regenerating passive film mediates improved resistance to combined wear and corrosion.
Mechanical wear exposes fresh alloy surfaces.
Freshly exposed HEA surfaces rapidly repassivate because of high configurational entropy and reactive elemental diversity.
Slight phase transformations at the wear interface promote dynamic repassivation.
Dynamic repassivation creates a self-healing surface layer that resists corrosion while being abraded.
The self-healing surface layer reduces overall degradation during tribocorrosion.
The degradation rate under combined wear and corrosion will be lower than the sum of degradation measured in isolated wear and isolated corrosion tests.
Wear depth during combined wear and corrosion will be moderately lower than under the isolated-wear baseline.
Corrosion penetration during combined wear and corrosion will be moderately lower than under the isolated-corrosion baseline.
The prediction should hold for HEAs with comparable metastable microstructures and chemical complexity.
The prediction may fail for alloys dominated by intermetallic phases.
The prediction may fail for alloys optimized exclusively for either wear resistance or corrosion resistance.
The magnitude of degradation reduction and the effectiveness of passive-film reformation may vary with mechanical load and electrolyte concentration.
